verdicts.correctedClaim: engine.test.ts gates positions at 180/540/720 arcsec while measured residuals against its own literals are 0.019-14.77 arcsec, so the gate is 12x (Neptune) to about 9400x (Mercury) looser than the residual and would pass a ~3 arcminute regression in any planet. verdicts.evidence: All Delta-T numbers reproduce to 0.001 s: astronomy-engine MakeTime tt-ut = 70.320 (2017-08-21), 71.578 (2020-01-01), 74.007 (2024-04-08), 75.497 (2026-09-22), 202.652 (2100), 717.161 (2300); IERS finals2000A Bulletin A UT1-UTC +0.3400 (I), -0.1772 (I), -0.0159 (I), -0.0117 (P) -> TT-UT1 68.844, 69.361, 69.200, 69.196; pyswisseph 2.10.03 deltat_ex 68.847, 69.361, 69.075, 68.821 (0.003-0.375 s from IERS). Cause confirmed: @zodiacs/engine dist/chunk-GBH7JIYF.js calls MakeTime(date) at lines 39/47/51/125 and never calls SetDeltaTFunction, and astronomy-engine's default DeltaT is DeltaT_EspenakMeeus (astronomy.js:1023,1141). No engine or time test asserts a Delta-T value; the only match is a comment at engine.test.ts:114. Correction: the finding's corroboration 'visible in the 2024 eclipse anchor: engine TT residual 4.18 s' is a misattribution. eTT = UTC_min + DeltaT_AE is exactly the TT at which the engine's ephemeris was evaluated, so eTT minus canon TT is Delta-T-independent ephemeris geometry (the engine's Moon-Sun separation minimum is 4.18 s late in TT, about 2.3 arcsec of relative longitude). The Delta-T error shows up in the UT residual, where it cancels against that geometry error to +0.87 s (anchors.json engine_UT_minus_canon_UT_s). Consistently, my venus-swiss.log check at 2024-04-08 18:17:18.3 UT finds the engine Moon only 0.72 arcsec from Swiss calc_ut despite a 4.9 s Delta-T difference (2.7 arcsec expected from Delta-T alone). The 1.2-3.5 arcsec figures are therefore the Delta-T component, not the total Moon error at any given instant.
verdicts.correctedClaim: The shipped engine converts UTC to TT with astronomy-engine's default Espenak-Meeus polynomial (no SetDeltaTFunction override), which is +1.5 s (2017), +2.2 s (2020), +4.8 s (2024) and +6.3 s (2026-09-22) ahead of IERS TT-UT1 and diverging about 1.2 s/yr, while Swiss 2.10.03 is within 0.4 s; no test asserts any Delta-T value. This is a systematic 1.2-3.5 arcsec Moon-longitude component today, partly masked at present by an opposite-sign error in astronomy-engine's Moon geometry (e.g. 0.72 arcsec total vs Swiss at the 2024 eclipse instant). The 2024 eclipse TT residual of 4.18 s is ephemeris geometry, not Delta-T, and should not be cited as evidence for this finding.

verdicts.evidence: Re-ran anchors.mjs (0.35 s) and swiss-anchors.py in my scratch: every number matches the auditor's to 0.01 s. TT residuals engine/alpha/Swiss: 2017 eclipse 1.51/1.15/1.14; 2024 eclipse 4.18/0.68/0.69; Venus 2004 16.76/0.74/0.87; Venus 2012 21.07/0.69/0.89; min separations engine 627.25/553.92, alpha 626.89/554.37, Swiss 626.89/554.37 vs canon 627/554. Swiss return flag asserted FLG_SWIEPH and not MOSEPH. Canon values verified in the cached NASA pages: SE2017Aug21Tpath.html 'Greatest Eclipse: 18:25:31.8 UT', SE2024Apr08Tpath.html '18:17:18.3 UT', SE2001-2100.html catalog 18:26:40 and 18:18:29 (TD), transit04.html 'Greatest 08:19:44' and '627 arc-seconds', transit12.html 'Greatest 01:29:36' and '554 arc-seconds', with transit12.html defining greatest transit as closest approach to the Sun's centre from Earth's centre. Independent cross-check (venus-swiss.log): at the canon UT instants the engine's Venus-minus-Sun relative longitude differs from Swiss calc_ut by +1.168 arcsec (2004) and +1.272 arcsec (2012), same sign, which at the measured -0.066 arcsec/s relative rate is 17.7 s and 19.3 s -- agreeing with the auditor's 16.35/19.49 s UT residuals and '1.1-1.4 arcsec, both in the same direction'. Note for readers: the eclipse TT residuals are pure ephemeris geometry; in UT the shipped engine lands -0.61 s and +0.87 s from canon UT because its Delta-T error cancels its Moon geometry error, so the Venus transits, not the eclipses, are the discriminating anchors for the shipped engine.

verdicts.correctedClaim: CI exercises the engine only through 'npm test' (vitest run, Node 22) and the alpha's tier-a node:test suite (site-check.yml:145-146 and :153-155); no workflow runs tier-b (85 tests, needs PRECISION_PACK; 84/85 pass in an out-of-tree copy here, the one failure being an import of a docs/ path that exists only in the full tree, 85/85 in the toolchain auditor's in-tree run), the 180-case Swiss benchmark, any Delta-T check, or any observational anchor. notes: Conventions checked: Horizons QUANTITIES=31 with CENTER=500@399 is apparent geocentric ecliptic-of-date lon/lat (matches engine.test.ts:4-5 and the engine's output); Swiss calls used FLG_SWIEPH with the return flag asserted (never Moshier); Swiss anchors in ET/TT via swe.calc, cross-checks in UT via swe.calc_ut; IERS TT-UT1 = 32.184 + 37 - (UT1-UTC) valid for all four dates (post-2017 leap second); 2026-09-22 IERS row is flagged P (predicted). No Horizons requests were made by this verifier (0 of 8); the auditor's cached responses were read instead. Side observation outside the assigned findings: examples/precision-alpha/tools/spk-backend.mjs imports ../../docs/platform/evidence/precision-2026-09-20/numerics/src/spk2.mjs, so the tier-b pack-versus-kernel test cannot run from the packaged alpha alone (package.json 'files' excludes docs/) -- relevant to any plan to run tier-b in CI from an archive.
